cohort_total_n_excerpt: We therefore examined this relation in a cohort of 43,432 men who were members of a prepaid health plan in northern California (United States) and who had received a health examination in the period from 1979 through 1985.
reason: The cohort evaluated prostate cancer developing after the health examination, but the abstract does not report an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Alcohol consumption was associated with no elevated prostate cancer risk for the 238 men in our study in whom prostate cancer developed, but smoking one or more packs of cigarettes per day was associated with an adjusted relative risk (RR) of 1.9 (95 percent confidence interval [CI] = 1.2-3.1).
estimate_classifications.reason: The alcohol result concerns prostate cancer generally, with no aggressive endpoint specified and no numeric alcohol effect estimate reported.
